data.title: Tethys Petroleum Press Release: Corporate Update on Operations and Kazakhstan Enforcement Proceedings
data.description:
Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands--(Newsfile Corp. - November 23, 2026) - Tethys Petroleum Limited ("Tethys" or the "Company") provides an update on developments in Kazakhstan concerning the enforcement of security over assets owned by TethysAralGas LLP ("TAG"), including an auction scheduled for November 26, 2026, and the Company's efforts to recover amounts owed by Special Financial Company DSFK LLP ("DSFK").

Operational update

The second gas compressor purchased by the Company has been installed at the Kul-Bas Central Processing Facility and has completed commissioning. Average oil production prior to installation of the compressor was 455 tons per day and is expected to increase to about 575 tons per day (4,577 bopd). Start-up testing has increased daily production to 550 tons per day.

Construction of additional phases of the Central Processing Facility increasing production storage and handling capacities are expected to be completed ahead of schedule before the end of the year.

Ontario Court Ruling

On November 13, 2026, the Ontario Superior Court of Justice dismissed a motion brought by Fincraft Group LLP ("Fincraft"), and supported by Eurasia Gazexport LLP and Olisol, seeking a finding that Tethys entities had breached, and were in contempt of, an existing Ontario court order in connection with the Company's 2026 Annual General Meeting. The Court announced its decision at the close of the hearing, and indicated that the principal issues in dispute between the parties should be litigated in the Cayman Islands rather than in Canada. Tethys has made submissions seeking an award of its costs of the motion. The existing Ontario order remains in place.

TAG's Pledged Assets and Cassation Ruling

In 2012, TAG pledged certain gas pipelines and related infrastructure as security for borrowings by Eurasia Gas Group LLP ("EGG") from Bank RBK. TAG was not the borrower, and the underlying loan claims were later assigned to DSFK. Under a December 2019 Settlement Deed and Release among Tethys, TAG, DSFK, EGG, Olisol Petroleum Limited ("Olisol"), Gemini IT Consultants DMCC and other parties, TAG was to be released from the pledges once DSFK received a settlement payment of approximately KZT 1.435 billion and Tethys issued 18 million ordinary shares to Olisol. TAG made the payment and Tethys issued the shares, but the mediation agreement approved by Kazakhstan's Supreme Court in May 2020 also made the release conditional on EGG arranging a pledge of Tethys shares in favour of DSFK. That share pledge was never completed, and DSFK did not release TAG's assets. DSFK has since continued enforcement under the mediation agreement. After the private bailiff authorized TAG to arrange an independent sale in December 2025, TAG agreed in January 2026 to sell the assets to its affiliate, Kul-Bas LLP, for approximately KZT 1.076 billion. That price was 75% of the KZT 1.435 billion value set in the mediation agreement, reflecting the maximum discount permitted by statute for an independent sale, and was above an independent valuation of approximately KZT 1.067 billion. Kul-Bas paid the full purchase price to the private bailiff in February 2026, but the bailiff rejected the transaction, citing the valuation and sale procedure, and returned the funds. On May 28, 2026, the bailiff ordered the assets transferred for forced sale. On July 10, 2026, a Kazakhstan administrative court set aside that order, finding that the required procedures had not been followed and that TAG had not been given a proper opportunity to complete the independent sale; this decision was upheld on appeal on August 21, 2026. On November 9, 2026, however, Kazakhstan's Cassation Court for Administrative Cases reversed both decisions and dismissed TAG's claim. It held that no new valuation was needed because the sale values had already been established under the mediation agreement, and that TAG had exhausted its one-time statutory right to arrange an independent sale even though that sale was never completed and the funds were returned. As a result, the private bailiff's order directing the forced sale of the pledged assets remains in effect.

Auction Scheduled for November 26, 2026

On November 16, 2026, the private bailiff published a notice of an electronic auction of TAG's pledged assets scheduled for November 26, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. local time in Aktobe. The assets are offered as a single lot comprising two gas pipelines of approximately 45.15 km and 4.85 km, non-residential premises in Bozoy, and Booster Compressor Stations Nos. 1 and 2. The advertised starting price is KZT 1,434,692,762, the aggregate value stated in the May 2020 mediation agreement.

On November 17, 2026, TAG received a decision of the private bailiff refusing its application to terminate the enforcement proceedings. The Company continues to question the continuation of enforcement without receiving sufficient supporting documents to verify the current outstanding balance of the underlying EGG indebtedness secured by TAG's assets. The Company has instructed its Kazakhstan legal counsel to challenge the auction and seek its suspension, and is considering other available legal remedies. There can be no assurance that the auction will be suspended or postponed.

Outstanding EGG Indebtedness

Under the May 2020 mediation agreement, EGG was scheduled to repay approximately KZT 4.719 billion to DSFK by December 2022. Despite requests, DSFK has not provided sufficient supporting information to enable Tethys to verify the amount still payable, including whether any amounts have since been repaid, settled or otherwise discharged, and the November 9 cassation ruling did not determine that balance. Tethys continues to pursue available legal remedies to establish the outstanding indebtedness and to challenge the continued enforcement against TAG's pledged assets.

Potential Operational Impact

The pledged gas pipelines and related infrastructure are used in TAG's gas production and transportation operations. The assets may be sold to a third party or, following an unsuccessful auction, transferred to DSFK under applicable enforcement procedures, and either outcome could affect TAG's continued access to and use of this infrastructure. Tethys is evaluating legal and commercial measures to protect its interests and maintain continuity of operations. The auction is currently scheduled for November 26, 2026, but its timing, outcome and possible operational and financial consequences remain uncertain.

Enforcement of Awards Against DSFK and Other Parties

As previously announced, on May 13, 2025, the International Arbitration Centre at the Astana International Financial Centre ("IAC") issued an award declaring the December 2019 Settlement Deed no longer binding between the parties to the arbitration, ordering DSFK to repay approximately KZT 1.435 billion and ordering cancellation of the share certificates representing the 18 million shares issued to Olisol. The AIFC Court subsequently dismissed challenges to the award and confirmed its enforceability.

Tethys continues to pursue enforcement of the IAC award and related AIFC Court orders against DSFK, Olisol Petroleum Limited, Eurasia Gazexport LLP, Alexander Abramov and Fedor Ossinin, as applicable under the respective decisions. In addition to repayment of approximately KZT 1.435 billion by DSFK, the awards and orders provide for interest and reimbursement of arbitration and legal costs, with liabilities varying among the parties.

While recoveries to date have been limited, the Company continues to pursue available enforcement measures to recover the outstanding amounts.

About Tethys

Tethys is focused on oil and gas exploration and production activities in Central Asia.

Certain statements in this release may constitute forward-looking information, including statements regarding anticipated production improvements, facility upgrades, pending legal proceedings in Kazakhstan and Canada, any possible suspension or outcome of the scheduled auction, continued access to infrastructure and recovery of amounts awarded to the Company. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to operational, financial, regulatory and legal uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially. data.title: Quebecor 'Encouraged' After Initial Talks With Telus
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Quebecor said its chief executive, Pierre-Karl Peladeau, met with his Telus counterpart on Monday, and was encouraged with a willingness to pursue further talks on a possible tieup.

Peladeau's meeting with Telus CEO Victor Dodig emerged one week after Quebecor unveiled a $22 billion bid to acquire the telecom rival. Quebecor has argued a deal with Telus would create a formidable Canadian-based telecom with the financial and technological wherewithal to counter a pending threat from space firms for wireless phone consumers.

Peladeau "is pleased that the discussion was initiated between both companies' top executives, and encouraged to see a willingness to pursue it," Quebecor said in a 53-word statement sent via email. The statement added that the two sides have agreed to keep discussion confidential.

A spokesman for Telus did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Telus said executive and board members have identified elevated risks with the proposed transaction, tied to regulatory approval. Quebecor is offering stock-and-cash to Telus shareholders.

Canadian antitrust and telecommunications regulators would need to sign off on Quebecor-Telus tieup. Canadian officials have in recent years highlighted the need to improve competition in certain sectors, such as telecommunications and banking.

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: Fed's Williams keeping options open on pace of future US rate hikes
data.description:
By Michael S. Derby

Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said Monday that while the economy’s performance will drive what the central bank does with monetary policy, he’s not ruling out steady rate increases if that’s what’s needed.

“I don't have in my mind a particular timing” when it comes to more US rate hikes, Williams told reporters after a speech before the University of Mount Saint Vincent. “We're going to have to learn along the way as we get more data,” the official said, while noting, “I'm not excluding options” and “I would not exclude, you know, moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed.”

data.title: Fed's Williams Won't Rule Out Consecutive Rate Hikes — Market Talk
data.description: The Fed needs to take further action to tame elevated inflation--and if price increases remain persistent, rate hikes at back-to-back meetings aren't out of the question, New York Fed President John Williams says. In a speech at University of Mount St. Vincent in the Bronx, Williams says, "we must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis." Speaking to reporters afterwards, he says those actions could include back-to-back rate hikes, which would mark an accelerated pace of tightening after the Fed skipped following September's rate increase with another in October. "I would not exclude ... moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed, if that's what the information was telling us," Williams says. (matt.grossman@wsj.com; @mattgrossman)

data.title: Jacobs Solutions Q4 Earnings Rise
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Jacobs Solutions Inc. (J) on Monday, reported higher net earnings for the quarter ended October 2, 2026, as a strong increase in revenue lifted its results compared with the corresponding period last year.

Net earnings attributable to Jacobs rose to $165.5 million from $122.3 million in the prior-year quarter. Earnings per share increased to $1.40 from $0.92, while revenue climbed 49.4 percent to $4.712 billion from $3.155 billion. Operating profit also advanced to $331.6 million from $211.6 million.

For fiscal 2026, net earnings attributable to Jacobs reached $381.7 million, compared with $289.3 million in fiscal 2025. Revenue increased to $15.777 billion from $12.030 billion, while earnings per share improved to $3.34 from $2.38.

For fiscal 2027, Jacobs expects adjusted net revenue of $10.0 billion to $10.35 billion and adjusted EPS of $8.05 to $8.45. It also forecasts an adjusted EBITDA margin of 15.4 percent to 15.7 percent and a free cash flow margin of 8.5 percent to 9.5 percent.

data.title: Intuitive Machines Advances Space Nuclear Systems to Enable Lunar Night Survival
data.description:
Successful START preliminary design review advances space nuclear technology toward flight and future lunar night survival

HOUSTON, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Intuitive Machines, Inc. (“Intuitive Machines”, together with its subsidiaries, the “Company”), a space infrastructure technology and services leader, today announced the successful completion of the preliminary design review for the Stirling Technology spAce Research experimenT (START). The successful review is a key milestone for START, which is being developed by Intuitive Machines in partnership with the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory’s (AFRL) Space Operations via Nuclear Enhanced Technology (SONET) team.

Conceptual rendering of the Stirling Technology spAce Research experimenT (START)

This collaboration between commercial industry and the Department of the Air Force aims to mature compact nuclear power technology toward flight readiness, benefitting America’s national space enterprise. It also advances Intuitive Machines’ strategically important development of space nuclear systems designed to enable longer-duration operations on the Moon and in deep space.

The partnership is part of Intuitive Machines’ previously announced $8.2 million contract extension from the AFRL/RJ to advance compact nuclear power technology toward flight readiness. The program is developing technologies intended to overcome the limitations of solar power and enable longer-duration missions on the Moon and deep space.

“Surviving the lunar night is a fundamental infrastructure challenge we have to solve if we want to operate on the Moon for weeks, months, and eventually years,” said Tim Crain, co-founder and CTO for Intuitive Machines. “Intuitive Machines is advancing space nuclear systems to provide the heat and power capabilities needed to extend mission duration and support sustained operations on the Moon for our customers.”

A lunar night lasts approximately 14 Earth days, creating prolonged periods without sunlight and exposing surface systems to extreme cold. These conditions present a fundamental challenge for spacecraft designed around solar power and batteries and limit how long systems can operate on the lunar surface.

START is designed to demonstrate Stirling power conversion technology in space, converting heat from a radioisotope source into electricity. As part of the AFRL/RJ program, the technology is slated to fly to the International Space Station (ISS) through the ISS National Laboratory in early 2028, using electrical power from the space station to simulate the heat from a radioisotope nuclear source.

About Intuitive Machines

Intuitive Machines is a next-generation space infrastructure company delivering integrated capabilities that build mission-critical spacecraft and systems, connect networks, and operate space infrastructure across Earth orbit, cislunar space, and deep space. Serving commercial, civil, and national security customers, the company enables resilient, scalable infrastructure that supports sustained exploration, communications, security, and commerce beyond Earth.

data.description:
PRELIMINARY PROSPECTUS ACCESSIBLE ON SEDAR+

NOT FOR RELEASE OR DISTRIBUTION IN THE UNITED STATES OR FOR DISSEMINATION TO U.S. NEWS WIRE SERVICES

TORONTO, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Conavi Medical Corp. (TSXV: CNVI) (“Conavi Medical” or the “Company”), a commercial stage medical device company focused on designing, manufacturing, and marketing imaging technologies to guide common minimally invasive cardiovascular procedures, announced today that it has filed a preliminary short form prospectus (the “Preliminary Prospectus”) with the securities regulatory authorities in the Provinces of British Columbia, Alberta and Ontario in connection with an offering (the “Offering”) of common shares of the Company (“Common Shares”) and/or pre-funded common share purchase warrants of the Company (“Pre-Funded Warrants” and, together with the Common Shares, the “Securities”) in lieu of Common Shares.

The Offering is expected to be completed on a commercially reasonable efforts agency basis pursuant to an agency agreement to be entered into between the Company and Bloom Burton Securities Inc. (“Bloom Burton” or the “Agent”). The number of Securities to be distributed, the size of the Offering and the price of each Common Share and Pre-Funded Warrant will be determined by negotiation between the Company and Bloom Burton in the context of the market with final terms to be determined at the time of pricing.

The Company intends to use the net proceeds from the Offering to complete a targeted market release in the United States of the Company’s OCTIV™ hybrid imaging system. The Company also intends to use the net proceeds for working capital and other general corporate purposes.

The Offering is expected to close on or about December 4, 2026 (the “Closing Date”) or such later date as may be agreed upon by the Company and Bloom Burton. The Offering is subject to the Company and the Agent entering into a definitive agency agreement, and subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including the receipt of all necessary regulatory and stock exchange approvals, including approval of the TSX Venture Exchange (“TSXV”).

In addition, the Securities are anticipated to be offered by way of private placement in certain jurisdictions outside of Canada pursuant to and in compliance with applicable securities laws.

data.title: Linamar to Acquire Terex's Aerials Unit for $1.4B
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Linamar will acquire Terex's aerials business, including the well-known Genie brand, for $1.4 billion in cash.

The business unit designs and manufactures lifts, telehandlers and elevated work platforms. The deal, which is expected to close in the first half, includes all assets, intellectual property and manufacturing sites under the unit.

The Canadian manufacturing firm said Monday the business will be added to its industrial segment, joining its lifts brand Skyjack. The brands will continue to operate separately, but Linamar expects the deal to eventually lead to savings of about $135 million a year.

Linamar also expects Genie will add about $2.3 billion of revenue on a last 12-months basis to segment revenue. The deal is being financed through a new credit facility with National Bank of Canada.

Terex, also a manufacturer, said the deal was part of its efforts to transform its business. The exited its tower and rough terrain cranes business in 2025, and acquired an environmental solutions unit in 2024. After the sale is completed the company will have three operating segments: environmental solutions, materials processing and specialty vehicles.

Proceeds from the deal to reduce net debt, return capital and support growth investments, Terex said.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com
